title: Choose where and how OBS records
summary: Set the Recording Path and Recording Format in Settings, Output.

steps.say: Make sure the Controls panel says Start Recording, not Stop Recording. Say done when it does.
hints: If it says Stop Recording, click it first.
Recording settings are locked while a recording is running.
steps.why: OBS grays out output settings during a recording.

steps.say: Click Settings in the Controls panel.
hints: It is above the Exit button at the bottom right.
Or open the File menu and choose Settings.
steps.why: Recording options live in the Settings window.

steps.say: Click Output in the list on the left.

checks.prompt: Is the Output page of OBS Settings showing, with a Recording section?

hints: Output is the third item, under General and Stream.
Press the Down arrow in the left list until Output is selected.
steps.why: The Output page controls file location, format and quality.

steps.say: In the Recording section, click Browse next to Recording Path and pick a folder.

checks.prompt: Does the Recording Path box show a different folder than before?

hints: Your Videos folder is a good choice because you can find it again from any app.
You can also click inside the Recording Path box and type a folder path.
steps.why: Knowing the folder means you can always find your recordings.

steps.say: Open the Recording Format dropdown and choose Hybrid MP4, or MKV if Hybrid MP4 is not listed.

checks.prompt: Is the Recording Format dropdown set to Hybrid MP4 or MKV?

hints: Hybrid MP4 survives a crash and plays almost everywhere.
Plain MP4 can be lost entirely if OBS crashes, so avoid it for long recordings.
steps.why: A crash-safe format protects hours of recording from a sudden power cut.

steps.say: Click OK to save your recording settings.
hints: OK is at the bottom right of the Settings window.
steps.why: Settings are not kept until you confirm them.
